options.text: The deployed set of resources created from a template, managed as a single unit

questions.explanation: A stack is the collection of resources CloudFormation provisions from a template and manages together — create, update, and delete apply to the whole stack.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of Infrastructure as Code? Select all that apply.

options.text: Easier disaster recovery by rebuilding from the template
It removes the need for any AWS permissions

questions.explanation: IaC gives repeatability, version control, and easy rebuilds. It does not remove permission requirements — deployments still act under IAM.

questions.prompt: What does a change set let you do?

options.text: Preview exactly what a stack update will add, modify, or replace before applying it

questions.explanation: A change set previews the effects of an update — including risky replacements — so you can confirm before applying.

questions.prompt: CloudFormation templates are written in YAML or ____ (the other supported format).
questions.explanation: CloudFormation templates can be authored in YAML or JSON; both declaratively describe the desired resources.

questions.prompt: You deployed via CloudFormation, then someone edited a resource by hand in the Console. What is this called, and how do you detect it?

options.text: A change set; detected by rollback
A stack policy; detected by CloudTrail only
It is impossible to change resources by hand

questions.explanation: Manual changes to IaC-managed resources cause drift; CloudFormation's drift detection reports where the real state differs from the template.

questions.prompt: How does the AWS CDK relate to CloudFormation?

options.text: You write infrastructure in a real programming language and it synthesizes CloudFormation underneath
It replaces CloudFormation with a database

questions.explanation: The CDK lets you define infrastructure in languages like TypeScript or Python and generates CloudFormation templates, running on the same engine.
